name: Amblyopia

category.name: Eye
category.part: AME Physical Examination Information and Disposition Tables

what_to_bring: Complete eye evaluation by a board-certified ophthalmologist which specifically includes if there is evidence of any other eye pathology.
Copies of testing already performed for any eye condition(s).

rows.label: A
rows.condition: Amblyopia or decreased distant vision which meets all the following: • Simple Refractive or Strabismic • One eye only • Unaffected eye Distance Vision is 20/20 or better (for all classes) Decreased vision caused by a process strictly limited to one eye with a fully normal fellow eye and an onset consistent with developmental adaptation
rows.condition_html:
A. Amblyopia or decreased distant vision which meets all the following:

• Simple Refractive or Strabismic

• One eye only

• Unaffected eye Distance Vision is 20/20 or better (for all classes)

Decreased vision caused by a process strictly limited to one eye with a fully normal fellow eye and an onset consistent with developmental adaptation
rows.evaluation_data: Submit the following for FAA review: - 1. Amblyopia Status Summary OR a current, detailed Clinical Progress Note generated from a clinic visit with their treating ophthalmologist or optometrist no more than 90 days before the AME exam which addresses all items on the Status Summary. - 2. Any associated progress notes.
rows.evaluation_data_html:

  • 2. Any associated progress notes.
rows.disposition: DEFER Summarize findings in Item 60. Submit the information to the FAA. In Item 60, specify the airman’s preferred FSDO if a Medical Flight Test (MFT) is required.

rows.label: B
rows.condition: All others - Any “Yes*” items on the Amblyopia Status Summary - Both eyes affected - Not congenital/early childhood and adapted - Any other eye disease - Medication use - Concerns/unstable vision - Does not meet 20/20 DVA in unaffected eye - Both eyes fail to achieve corrected normal vision because of refractive errors (high hyperopia, myopia, or astigmatism).
rows.condition_html:
B. All others

  • Any “Yes*” items on the Amblyopia Status Summary
  • Both eyes affected
  • Not congenital/early childhood and adapted
  • Any other eye disease
  • Medication use
  • Concerns/unstable vision
  • Does not meet 20/20 DVA in unaffected eye
  • Both eyes fail to achieve corrected normal vision because of refractive errors (high hyperopia, myopia, or astigmatism).
